body.en: Topic 2 establishes the structural theory of functions: domain-range mappings, injectivity and invertibility criteria, composite systems, transformation algebra, and analysis of rational, quadratic, exponential, and logarithmic families.
body.ar: Topic 2 establishes the structural theory of الدوال: المجال-المدى mappings, injectivity and invertibility criteria, composite systems, transformation الجبر, and analysis of rational, quadratic, exponential, and logarithmic families.

label.en: ● Level 1 Foundation — Function Concepts, Inverses & Composites
label.ar: ● Level 1 Foundation — الدالة Concepts, Inverses & Composites

body.en:
A function \(f: X \to Y\) is a relation assigning to each input element \(x \in X\) (the domain) exactly one output element \(y \in Y\). The range (image) is the set \(f(X) = \{f(x) \mid x \in X\} \subseteq Y\).

  • Injectivity (One-to-One): \(f(x_1) = f(x_2) \implies x_1 = x_2\). Graphically verified by the horizontal line test: every horizontal line intersects the graph at most once.
  • Surjectivity (Onto): For every \(y \in Y\), there exists \(x \in X\) such that \(f(x) = y\). A function is bijective if it is both injective and surjective.
  • Composite Functions: Given \(g: A \to B\) and \(f: B \to C\), the composite function \((f \circ g)(x) = f(g(x))\) is defined for all \(x \in \text{dom}(g)\) such that \(g(x) \in \text{dom}(f)\). In general, composition is non-commutative: \(f(g(x)) \neq g(f(x))\).
  • Inverse Functions: The inverse function \(f^{-1}\) exists if and only if \(f\) is bijective (one-to-one on its stated domain). By definition: \[ f(f^{-1}(x)) = x \quad \text{and} \quad f^{-1}(f(x)) = x. \] Graphically, the curve \(y = f^{-1}(x)\) is the reflection of \(y = f(x)\) in the line of symmetry \(y = x\). The domain of \(f^{-1}\) is the range of \(f\), and the range of \(f^{-1}\) is the domain of \(f\).
body.ar:
A function \(f: X \to Y\) is a relation assigning to each input element \(x \in X\) (the domain) exactly one output element \(y \in Y\). The range (image) is the set \(f(X) = \{f(x) \mid x \in X\} \subseteq Y\).

  • Injectivity (One-to-One): \(f(x_1) = f(x_2) \implies x_1 = x_2\). Graphically verified by the horizontal line test: every horizontal line intersects the التمثيل البياني at most once.
  • Surjectivity (Onto): For every \(y \in Y\), there exists \(x \in X\) such that \(f(x) = y\). A الدالة is bijective if it is both injective and surjective.
  • Composite الدوال: المعطيات \(g: A \to B\) and \(f: B \to C\), the composite الدالة \((f \circ g)(x) = f(g(x))\) is defined for all \(x \in \text{dom}(g)\) such that \(g(x) \in \text{dom}(f)\). In general, composition is non-commutative: \(f(g(x)) \neq g(f(x))\).
  • Inverse الدوال: The inverse الدالة \(f^{-1}\) exists if and only if \(f\) is bijective (one-to-one on its stated المجال). By definition: \[ f(f^{-1}(x)) = x \quad \text{and} \quad f^{-1}(f(x)) = x. \] Graphically, the curve \(y = f^{-1}(x)\) is the reflection of \(y = f(x)\) in the line of symmetry \(y = x\). The المجال of \(f^{-1}\) is the المدى of \(f\), and the المدى of \(f^{-1}\) is the المجال of \(f\).

body.en: Domain Restrictions, Invertibility & Asymptotic Behavior: An algebraic or transcendental function \(f: D \to R\) possesses an inverse \(f^{-1}: R \to D\) if and only if \(f\) is strictly one-to-one (bijective) on \(D\), guaranteeing that \(\text{dom}(f^{-1}) = \text{ran}(f)\) and \(\text{ran}(f^{-1}) = \text{dom}(f)\). For logarithmic and radical equations, every algebraic step that squares both sides or combines logs (\(\log_b u + \log_b v = \log_b(uv)\)) can enlarge the solution set, requiring a final domain check against the original equation.
body.ar: Domain Restrictions, Invertibility & Asymptotic Behavior: An algebraic or transcendental الدالة \(f: D \to R\) possesses an inverse \(f^{-1}: R \to D\) if and only if \(f\) is strictly one-to-one (bijective) on \(D\), guaranteeing that \(\text{dom}(f^{-1}) = \text{ran}(f)\) and \(\text{ran}(f^{-1}) = \text{dom}(f)\). For logarithmic and radical المعادلات, every algebraic step that squares both sides or combines logs (\(\log_b u + \log_b v = \log_b(uv)\)) can enlarge the الحل set, requiring a final المجال check against the original المعادلة.

label.en: ● Level 2 Analytical Tools — Transformation Algebra & Function Families
label.ar: ● Level 2 Analytical Tools — Transformation الجبر & الدالة Families

body.en:
Transformation System \(y = a f(b(x - h)) + k\):

  • Vertical Stretch by factor \(|a|\): \(y = a f(x)\). If \(a < 0\), also reflected across the \(x\)-axis (\(y = -f(x)\)).
  • Horizontal Stretch by factor \(1/|b|\): \(y = f(bx)\). If \(b < 0\), also reflected across the \(y\)-axis (\(y = f(-x)\)).
  • Horizontal Translation: \(y = f(x - h)\) shifts the curve right by \(h\) units (left if \(h < 0\)). Always factor the inside: \(f(bx - c) = f(b(x - c/b))\).
  • Vertical Translation: \(y = f(x) + k\) shifts the curve up by \(k\) units (down if \(k < 0\)).

Primary Function Families & Invariants:

  • Quadratic Family: \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c = a(x - h)^2 + k\). Vertex \((h, k) = \left(-\frac{b}{2a}, c - \frac{b^2}{4a}\right)\). Discriminant \(\Delta = b^2 - 4ac\) determines root multiplicity: \(\Delta > 0\) (two real roots), \(\Delta = 0\) (one repeated root), \(\Delta < 0\) (no real roots; if \(a > 0\), \(f(x) > 0\) globally).
  • Rational / Homographic Family: \(f(x) = \frac{ax + b}{cx + d}\) with \(c \neq 0\) and \(ad - bc \neq 0\).
    Vertical asymptote: \(x = -\frac{d}{c}\); Horizontal asymptote: \(y = \frac{a}{c}\); \(y\)-intercept: \((0, b/d)\); \(x\)-intercept: \((-b/a, 0)\).
  • Exponential & Logarithmic Families: \(f(x) = a k^x + c\) with horizontal asymptote \(y = c\); inverse \(g(x) = a \log_b(x - d) + c\) with vertical asymptote \(x = d\).

Transformation System \(y = a f(b(x - h)) + k\):

  • Vertical Stretch by factor \(|a|\): \(y = a f(x)\). If \(a < 0\), also reflected across the \(x\)-axis (\(y = -f(x)\)).
  • Horizontal Stretch by factor \(1/|b|\): \(y = f(bx)\). If \(b < 0\), also reflected across the \(y\)-axis (\(y = f(-x)\)).
  • Horizontal Translation: \(y = f(x - h)\) shifts the curve right by \(h\) units (left if \(h < 0\)). Always factor the inside: \(f(bx - c) = f(b(x - c/b))\).
  • Vertical Translation: \(y = f(x) + k\) shifts the curve up by \(k\) units (down if \(k < 0\)).

Primary الدالة Families & Invariants:

  • Quadratic Family: \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c = a(x - h)^2 + k\). الرأس \((h, k) = \left(-\frac{b}{2a}, c - \frac{b^2}{4a}\right)\). Discriminant \(\Delta = b^2 - 4ac\) determines root multiplicity: \(\Delta > 0\) (two real roots), \(\Delta = 0\) (one repeated root), \(\Delta < 0\) (no real roots; if \(a > 0\), \(f(x) > 0\) globally).
  • Rational / Homographic Family: \(f(x) = \frac{ax + b}{cx + d}\) with \(c \neq 0\) and \(ad - bc \neq 0\).
    Vertical خط التقارب: \(x = -\frac{d}{c}\); Horizontal خط التقارب: \(y = \frac{a}{c}\); \(y\)-المقطع: \((0, b/d)\); \(x\)-المقطع: \((-b/a, 0)\).
  • Exponential & Logarithmic Families: \(f(x) = a k^x + c\) with horizontal خط التقارب \(y = c\); inverse \(g(x) = a \log_b(x - d) + c\) with vertical خط التقارب \(x = d\).

label.en: ● Level 3 University Rigor — Rational Inverses, Self-Inverse Proofs & Asymptotes
label.ar: ● Level 3 University Rigor — Rational Inverses, Self-Inverse Proofs & خطوط التقارب

body.en:
Theorem (Rational Function Inverse): Let \(f(x) = \frac{ax + b}{cx + d}\) with \(ad - bc \neq 0\) on domain \(\mathbb{R} \setminus \{-d/c\}\). Then the inverse function is:

\[ f^{-1}(x) = \frac{-dx + b}{cx - a} \quad \text{on domain } \mathbb{R} \setminus \{a/c\}. \]

Proof: Set \(y = \frac{ax + b}{cx + d}\). Clear denominators: \(y(cx + d) = ax + b \implies cxy + dy = ax + b\).
Group \(x\) terms: \(cxy - ax = b - dy \implies x(cy - a) = -dy + b\).
Solve for \(x\): \[ x = \frac{-dy + b}{cy - a}. \]
Swapping variables yields \(f^{-1}(x) = \frac{-dx + b}{cx - a}\). ∎

Corollary (Self-Inverse Criterion): A rational function \(f(x) = \frac{ax + b}{cx + d}\) is self-inverse (i.e. \(f(f(x)) = x\) for all \(x\)) if and only if \(a = -d\). When \(a = -d\), the vertical asymptote \(x = a/c\) and horizontal asymptote \(y = a/c\) intersect at a point lying precisely on the axis of symmetry \(y = x\).
body.ar:
Theorem (Rational الدالة Inverse): Let \(f(x) = \frac{ax + b}{cx + d}\) with \(ad - bc \neq 0\) on المجال \(\mathbb{R} \setminus \{-d/c\}\). Then the inverse الدالة is:

\[ f^{-1}(x) = \frac{-dx + b}{cx - a} \quad \text{on domain } \mathbb{R} \setminus \{a/c\}. \]

Proof: Set \(y = \frac{ax + b}{cx + d}\). Clear denominators: \(y(cx + d) = ax + b \implies cxy + dy = ax + b\).
Group \(x\) terms: \(cxy - ax = b - dy \implies x(cy - a) = -dy + b\).
Solve for \(x\): \[ x = \frac{-dy + b}{cy - a}. \]
Swapping المتغيرات yields \(f^{-1}(x) = \frac{-dx + b}{cx - a}\). ∎

Corollary (Self-Inverse Criterion): A rational الدالة \(f(x) = \frac{ax + b}{cx + d}\) is self-inverse (i.e. \(f(f(x)) = x\) for all \(x\)) if and only if \(a = -d\). عندما \(a = -d\), the vertical خط التقارب \(x = a/c\) and horizontal خط التقارب \(y = a/c\) intersect at a point lying precisely on the axis of symmetry \(y = x\).

label.ar: ◆ لماذا تعمل هذه الطريقة رياضياً — First-Principles اشتقاق (الدوال)

body.en:
Why Completing the Square & Log-Linearization Work: Any quadratic \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) (\(a \ne 0\)) can be rewritten by factoring \(a\) from the first two terms and adding/subtracting \((b/2a)^2\):

\[ ax^2 + bx + c = a\!\left(x + \frac{b}{2a}\right)^2 + \left(c - \frac{b^2}{4a}\right) \]

Because \(\left(x + \frac{b}{2a}\right)^2 \ge 0\) for all \(x \in \mathbb{R}\), the extreme value \(k = c - \frac{b^2}{4a}\) is attained uniquely at the axis of symmetry \(x = -\frac{b}{2a}\), restricting the range to \([k, \infty)\) (if \(a > 0\)) and making \(f\) invertible on \(x \ge -\frac{b}{2a}\). Similarly, applying \(\ln\) to power laws \(y = ax^n\) yields \(\ln y = n\ln x + \ln a\), transforming a nonlinear curve into a straight line of gradient \(n\).

label.en: Worked Example 2.1 — Composite Functions & Domain Restrictions
label.ar: مثال محلول 2.1 — Composite الدوال & المجال Restrictions

problem.en:
Let \(f(x) = \sqrt{25 - x^2}\) and \(g(x) = \frac{3}{x - 1}\).
(a) Find the natural domain and range of \(f(x)\).
(b) Determine the exact expression and maximal domain for \((g \circ f)(x)\).
(c) Solve the equation \((g \circ f)(x) = 1\).
problem.ar:
Let \(f(x) = \sqrt{25 - x^2}\) and \(g(x) = \frac{3}{x - 1}\).
(a) أوجد natural المجال and المدى of \(f(x)\).
(b) حدّد exact العبارة الجبرية and maximal المجال for \((g \circ f)(x)\).
(c) حل المعادلة \((g \circ f)(x) = 1\).

solution.en:
(a) Domain of \(f\): \(25 - x^2 \ge 0 \implies x^2 \le 25 \implies [-5, 5]\). Since \(0 \le 25 - x^2 \le 25\), the range of \(f\) is \([0, 5]\).

(b) \((g \circ f)(x) = g(f(x)) = \frac{3}{\sqrt{25 - x^2} - 1}\).
Maximal domain requires \(x \in [-5, 5]\) and \(f(x) \neq 1\):
\[ \sqrt{25 - x^2} - 1 = 0 \implies 25 - x^2 = 1 \implies x^2 = 24 \implies x = \pm 2\sqrt{6}. \]
Thus, \(\text{dom}(g \circ f) = [-5, 5] \setminus \{-2\sqrt{6}, 2\sqrt{6}\}\).

(c) Solve \(\frac{3}{\sqrt{25 - x^2} - 1} = 1\):
\[ \sqrt{25 - x^2} - 1 = 3 \implies \sqrt{25 - x^2} = 4 \implies 25 - x^2 = 16 \implies x^2 = 9 \implies x = \pm 3. \]
Both \(x = 3\) and \(x = -3\) lie in the domain. The solutions are \(x = \pm 3\).
solution.ar:
(a) المجال of \(f\): \(25 - x^2 \ge 0 \implies x^2 \le 25 \implies [-5, 5]\). Since \(0 \le 25 - x^2 \le 25\), the المدى of \(f\) is \([0, 5]\).

(b) \((g \circ f)(x) = g(f(x)) = \frac{3}{\sqrt{25 - x^2} - 1}\).
Maximal المجال requires \(x \in [-5, 5]\) and \(f(x) \neq 1\):
\[ \sqrt{25 - x^2} - 1 = 0 \implies 25 - x^2 = 1 \implies x^2 = 24 \implies x = \pm 2\sqrt{6}. \]
Thus, \(\text{dom}(g \circ f) = [-5, 5] \setminus \{-2\sqrt{6}, 2\sqrt{6}\}\).

(c) Solve \(\frac{3}{\sqrt{25 - x^2} - 1} = 1\):
\[ \sqrt{25 - x^2} - 1 = 3 \implies \sqrt{25 - x^2} = 4 \implies 25 - x^2 = 16 \implies x^2 = 9 \implies x = \pm 3. \]
Both \(x = 3\) and \(x = -3\) lie in the المجال. The الحلول are \(x = \pm 3\).

problem.en:
Consider the function \(f(x) = \frac{4x - 7}{2x - 4}\) for \(x \neq 2\).
(a) Write down the equations of the vertical and horizontal asymptotes.
(b) Show that \(f\) is self-inverse.
(c) Find the coordinates of the points where the graph of \(y = f(x)\) intersects the line \(y = x\).
problem.ar:
Consider the الدالة \(f(x) = \frac{4x - 7}{2x - 4}\) for \(x \neq 2\).
(a) Write down the المعادلات of the vertical and horizontal خطوط التقارب.
(b) Show that \(f\) is self-inverse.
(c) أوجد إحداثيات the points حيث the التمثيل البياني of \(y = f(x)\) intersects the line \(y = x\).

solution.en:
(a) Vertical asymptote occurs where denominator is zero: \(2x - 4 = 0 \implies x = 2\).
Horizontal asymptote: \(y = \lim_{x\to\pm\infty} \frac{4x - 7}{2x - 4} = \frac{4}{2} = 2\).

(b) Using the rational inverse formula \(f^{-1}(x) = \frac{-dx + b}{cx - a}\) with \(a = 4, b = -7, c = 2, d = -4\):
\[ f^{-1}(x) = \frac{-(-4)x + (-7)}{2x - 4} = \frac{4x - 7}{2x - 4} = f(x). \]
Alternatively, evaluate \(f(f(x))\):
\[ f(f(x)) = \frac{4\left(\frac{4x-7}{2x-4}\right) - 7}{2\left(\frac{4x-7}{2x-4}\right) - 4} = \frac{4(4x - 7) - 7(2x - 4)}{2(4x - 7) - 4(2x - 4)} = \frac{16x - 28 - 14x + 28}{8x - 14 - 8x + 16} = \frac{2x}{2} = x. \]
Since \(f(f(x)) = x\), \(f\) is self-inverse. ∎

(c) Solve \(f(x) = x\):
\[ \frac{4x - 7}{2x - 4} = x \implies 4x - 7 = 2x^2 - 4x \implies 2x^2 - 8x + 7 = 0. \]
By quadratic formula: \[ x = \frac{8 \pm \sqrt{64 - 4(2)(7)}}{4} = \frac{8 \pm \sqrt{8}}{4} = 2 \pm \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}. \]
Points of intersection: \(\left(2 - \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}, 2 - \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)\) and \(\left(2 + \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}, 2 + \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)\).
solution.ar:
(a) Vertical خط التقارب occurs حيث denominator is zero: \(2x - 4 = 0 \implies x = 2\).
Horizontal خط التقارب: \(y = \lim_{x\to\pm\infty} \frac{4x - 7}{2x - 4} = \frac{4}{2} = 2\).

(b) Using the rational inverse الصيغة \(f^{-1}(x) = \frac{-dx + b}{cx - a}\) with \(a = 4, b = -7, c = 2, d = -4\):
\[ f^{-1}(x) = \frac{-(-4)x + (-7)}{2x - 4} = \frac{4x - 7}{2x - 4} = f(x). \]
Alternatively, احسب قيمة \(f(f(x))\):
\[ f(f(x)) = \frac{4\left(\frac{4x-7}{2x-4}\right) - 7}{2\left(\frac{4x-7}{2x-4}\right) - 4} = \frac{4(4x - 7) - 7(2x - 4)}{2(4x - 7) - 4(2x - 4)} = \frac{16x - 28 - 14x + 28}{8x - 14 - 8x + 16} = \frac{2x}{2} = x. \]
Since \(f(f(x)) = x\), \(f\) is self-inverse. ∎

(c) Solve \(f(x) = x\):
\[ \frac{4x - 7}{2x - 4} = x \implies 4x - 7 = 2x^2 - 4x \implies 2x^2 - 8x + 7 = 0. \]
By quadratic الصيغة: \[ x = \frac{8 \pm \sqrt{64 - 4(2)(7)}}{4} = \frac{8 \pm \sqrt{8}}{4} = 2 \pm \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}. \]
Points of التقاطع: \(\left(2 - \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}, 2 - \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)\) and \(\left(2 + \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}, 2 + \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)\).

label.en: ⚠ Topic 2 Exam Traps: Functions, Inverses & Transformations
label.ar: ⚠ Topic 2 Exam Traps: الدوال, Inverses & Transformations

body.en:
Horizontal Transformation Factoring: For \(y = f(2x - 6)\), always factor the argument as \(f(2(x - 3))\). This represents a horizontal compression by factor \(\frac{1}{2}\) followed by a translation right by 3 units (NOT 6).

Composite Evaluation Order: \((f \circ g)(x) = f(g(x))\) evaluates \(g\) first, then substitutes into \(f\). Never confuse \((f \circ g)(x)\) with the algebraic product \(f(x) \cdot g(x)\).

Domain Restriction for Inverses: A quadratic \(f(x) = (x-2)^2 + 1\) has no inverse on \(\mathbb{R}\) because it fails the horizontal line test. You must restrict the domain to \(x \ge 2\) (or \(x \le 2\)) before writing \(f^{-1}(x) = 2 + \sqrt{x - 1}\).
body.ar:

Domain Restriction for Inverses: A quadratic \(f(x) = (x-2)^2 + 1\) has no inverse on \(\mathbb{R}\) because it fails the horizontal line test. You must restrict the المجال to \(x \ge 2\) (or \(x \le 2\)) before writing \(f^{-1}(x) = 2 + \sqrt{x - 1}\).

Worked Example (AA SL Paper 1 — 7 marks):
Let \(f(x) = 2x^2 - 8x + k\). The graph of \(f\) has vertex \(V(2, -3)\).
(a) Show that \(k = 5\). [2]
(b) The graph of \(g\) is obtained by translating the graph of \(f\) by \(\binom{-1}{4}\) followed by a vertical stretch of scale factor \(2\). Find the coordinates of the vertex of \(g\). [3]
(c) State the range of \(g\). [2]

Official IB Markscheme Solution:
(a) Completing the square or evaluating \(f(2) = -3\): \(2(2)^2 - 8(2) + k = -3 \implies 8 - 16 + k = -3\) [M1] \(\implies k = 5\) [A1] [AG]
(b) Translation by \(\binom{-1}{4}\) moves \((2, -3) \to (2 - 1, -3 + 4) = (1, 1)\) [M1] [A1]; vertical stretch by factor \(2\) maps \((1, 1) \to (1, 2)\) [A1]
(c) Since \(a = 2 \times 2 = 4 > 0\), range is \(g(x) \ge 2\) (or \([2, \infty)\)) [M1] [A1]

question.en: Practice 2.1: The function \(f(x) = 3 - \ln(2x + 1)\) is defined for \(x > -0.5\). Find an expression for \(f^{-1}(x)\), state its domain and range, and write down the coordinates of the intercept of \(y = f^{-1}(x)\) with the \(y\)-axis.
question.ar: Practice 2.1: The function \(f(x) = 3 - \ln(2x + 1)\) is defined for \(x > -0.5\). أوجد an expression for \(f^{-1}(x)\), state its domain and range, and write down the coordinates of the intercept of \(y = f^{-1}(x)\) with the \(y\)-axis.

solution.en:
1. Let \(y = 3 - \ln(2x + 1)\).
2. Rearrange: \(\ln(2x + 1) = 3 - y \implies 2x + 1 = e^{3 - y} \implies x = \frac{e^{3 - y} - 1}{2}\).
3. Swap variables: \(f^{-1}(x) = \frac{e^{3 - x} - 1}{2}\).
4. Domain of \(f^{-1}\) is the range of \(f\), which is \(\mathbb{R}\) (all real numbers). Range of \(f^{-1}\) is the domain of \(f\), \((-0.5, \infty)\).
5. The \(y\)-intercept occurs at \(x = 0\): \(f^{-1}(0) = \frac{e^3 - 1}{2}\). Coordinates: \(\left(0, \frac{e^3 - 1}{2}\right)\).

4. Domain of \(f^{-1}\) is the range of \(f\), which is \(\mathbb{R}\) (all real numbers). Range of \(f^{-1}\) is the domain of \(f\), \((-0.5, \infty)\).
5. The \(y\)-intercept occurs at \(x = 0\): \(f^{-1}(0) = \frac{e^3 - 1}{2}\). Coordinates: \(\left(0, \frac{e^3 - 1}{2}\right)\).

question.en: Practice 2.2: The graph of \(y = f(x)\) undergoes three consecutive transformations: (1) a horizontal stretch by scale factor 3, (2) a reflection in the \(y\)-axis, and (3) a translation by vector \(\begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ -5 \end{pmatrix}\). Write down the equation of the resulting function \(g(x)\) in terms of \(f\).
question.ar: Practice 2.2: The graph of \(y = f(x)\) undergoes three consecutive transformations: (1) a horizontal stretch by scale حلّل 3, (2) a reflection in the \(y\)-axis, and (3) a translation by vector \(\begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ -5 \end{pmatrix}\). Write down the equation of the resulting function \(g(x)\) in terms of \(f\).

solution.en:
1. Horizontal stretch by factor 3: \(x \mapsto \frac{x}{3}\), giving \(y = f\left(\frac{x}{3}\right)\).
2. Reflection in \(y\)-axis: \(x \mapsto -x\), giving \(y = f\left(-\frac{x}{3}\right)\).
3. Translation by \(\begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ -5 \end{pmatrix}\): replace \(x\) by \(x - 4\) and subtract 5: \[ g(x) = f\left( -\frac{x - 4}{3} \right) - 5 = f\left( \frac{4 - x}{3} \right) - 5. \]

question.en: [Practice 3 · Medium] The graph of the quadratic function \( f(x) = 2x^2 - kx + 5 \) passes through the point (3, 14). Find the value of \( k \).

hints.en: The graph of the function \( f(x) = 2x^2 - kx + 5 \) passes through the point (3, 14). This means that when \( x = 3 \), \( f(x) = 14 \). We can substitute these values into the function's equation: \( 14 = 2(3)^2 - k(3) + 5 \).

أعد كتابة العلاقة وبسّطها للحصول على: \( 14 = 2(9) - 3k + 5 \) \( 14 = 18 - 3k + 5 \) \( 14 = 23 - 3k \).

question.en: [Practice 4 · Medium] The graph of the quadratic function \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) is shown below. The graph passes through the points \((1, 0)\), \((5, 0)\), and \((0, -10)\). Find the value of \(a\).
question.ar: [Practice 4 · Medium] The graph of the quadratic function \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) is shown below. The graph يمر بالنقطة the points \((1, 0)\), \((5, 0)\), and \((0, -10)\). أوجد قيمة \(a\).

hints.en: The quadratic function has roots at \(x=1\) and \(x=5\). Therefore, it can be written in the factored form \(f(x) = a(x-1)(x-5)\). We are given that the graph passes through the point \((0, -10)\). Substituting these coordinates into the factored form: \(-10 = a(0-1)(0-5)\).
hints.ar: The quadratic function has roots at \(x=1\) and \(x=5\). وبالتالي، it can be written in the حلّلed form \(f(x) = a(x-1)(x-5)\). We are إذا علمت أن the graph يمر بالنقطة the point \((0, -10)\). Substituting these coordinates into the حلّلed form: \(-10 = a(0-1)(0-5)\).

hints.en: Rewrite and simplify to obtain: \(-10 = a(-1)(-5)\) \(-10 = 5a\).
hints.ar: أعد كتابة العلاقة وبسّطها للحصول على: \(-10 = a(-1)(-5)\) \(-10 = 5a\).

hints.en: Dividing both sides by 5, we get \(a\).
hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(a\) لتبسيط الخطوة.

solution.en: The quadratic function has roots at \(x=1\) and \(x=5\). Therefore, it can be written in the factored form \(f(x) = a(x-1)(x-5)\). We are given that the graph passes through the point \((0, -10)\). Substituting these coordinates into the factored form: \(-10 = a(0-1)(0-5)\) \(-10 = a(-1)(-5)\) \(-10 = 5a\) Dividing both sides by 5, we get \(a = -2\).

question.en: Consider the function \( f(x) = 2x + 3 \). What is the value of \( f(4) \)?
question.ar: Consider the function \( f(x) = 2x + 3 \). ما قيمة \( f(4) \)?

hints.en: To find the value of \( f(4) \), we substitute \( x=4 \) into the function \( f(x) = 2x + 3 \).
hints.ar: To أوجد قيمة \( f(4) \), we عوّض \( x=4 \) into the function \( f(x) = 2x + 3 \).

hints.en: Rewrite and simplify to obtain: \( f(4) = 2(4) + 3 \).
hints.ar: أعد كتابة العلاقة وبسّطها للحصول على: \( f(4) = 2(4) + 3 \).

hints.en: Use the resulting form to finish: \(f(4) = 8 + 3\).

solution.en: To find the value of \( f(4) \), we substitute \( x=4 \) into the function \( f(x) = 2x + 3 \). \( f(4) = 2(4) + 3 \) \( f(4) = 8 + 3 \) \( f(4) = 11 \) [M1] [A1]

label.en: ● Master Atlas of the 9 Main Parent Functions & Universal Transformation Law
label.ar: ● الأطلس الشامل للدوال الأم التسع وقانون التحويلات الهندسية العام

body.en:
Every algebraic and elementary transcendental model is built by transforming one of the nine core parent functions via \(g(x) = a\,f(x - h) + k\), where \(|a|\) scales vertically (reflecting across the \(x\)-axis if \(a < 0\)), \(h\) shifts horizontally, and \(k\) shifts vertically:

FamilyTransformed Form \(g(x)\)DomainRange (\(a > 0\))Key Geometric Feature
Constant\(f(x) = c\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\(\{c\}\)Horizontal line, slope \(0\)
Linear\(a(x - h) + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)Constant slope \(m = a\), pivot \((h, k)\)
Quadratic\(a(x - h)^2 + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\([k, \infty)\)Parabola vertex \((h, k)\), axis \(x = h\)
Cubic\(a(x - h)^3 + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)Inflection center \((h, k)\), S-curve
Absolute Value\(a|x - h| + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\([k, \infty)\)V-corner vertex \((h, k)\), slopes \(\pm a\)
Radical\(a\sqrt{x - h} + k\)\([h, \infty)\)\([k, \infty)\)Endpoint \((h, k)\), half-parabola
Rational\(\dfrac{a}{x - h} + k\)\(x \neq h\)\(y \neq k\)Vertical asymptote \(x = h\), horizontal \(y = k\)
Exponential\(a \cdot 2^{x - h} + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((k, \infty)\)Horizontal asymptote \(y = k\), anchor \((h, a+k)\)
Logarithmic\(a\ln(x - h) + k\)\((h, \infty)\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)Vertical asymptote \(x = h\), anchor \((h+1, k)\)
body.ar:
تُبنى النماذج الجبرية والمتسامية الأساسية من خلال تطبيق التحويل القياسي \(g(x) = a\,f(x - h) + k\) على إحدى الدوال الأم التسع، حيث يتحكم \(|a|\) في التمدد الرأسي (مع انعكاس حول محور السينات إذا كان \(a < 0\))، ويمثل \(h\) الإزاحة الأفقية، و\(k\) الإزاحة الرأسية:

عائلة الدالةالصورة المحوّلة \(g(x)\)المجالالمدى (\(a > 0\))السمة الهندسية المميزة
الثابتة\(f(x) = c\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\(\{c\}\)مستقيم أفقي ميله \(0\)
الخطية\(a(x - h) + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)ميل ثابت \(m = a\) ونقطة ارتكاز \((h, k)\)
التربيعية\(a(x - h)^2 + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\([k, \infty)\)قطع مكافئ رأسه \((h, k)\) ومحوره \(x = h\)
التكعيبية\(a(x - h)^3 + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)نقطة انعطاف مركزية \((h, k)\)
القيمة المطلقة\(a|x - h| + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\([k, \infty)\)رأس زاوي على شكل V عند \((h, k)\) بميلين \(\pm a\)
الجذرية\(a\sqrt{x - h} + k\)\([h, \infty)\)\([k, \infty)\)نقطة بداية \((h, k)\) ومجال مقيّد \(x \ge h\)
النسبية (المقلوب)\(\dfrac{a}{x - h} + k\)\(x \neq h\)\(y \neq k\)تقارب رأسي \(x = h\) وتقارب أفقي \(y = k\)
الأسية\(a \cdot 2^{x - h} + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((k, \infty)\)تقارب أفقي \(y = k\) ونقطة ارتكاز \((h, a+k)\)
اللوغاريتمية\(a\ln(x - h) + k\)\((h, \infty)\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)تقارب رأسي \(x = h\) ونقطة ارتكاز \((h+1, k)\)
